correctness.rationale: Koopman contains a reducing bilateral-shift subspace, so has full circle spectrum; direct-integral resolvent reduces to every phase of the finite fiber. Positive bidiagonal inverse entries have a single path and separable row-column signs, proving an exact real-radius maximum in the induced 2-norm. The smaller 2x2 squared singular value is an explicit function decreasing in squared distance from the radial midpoint, and exterior monotonicity proves the connected-component dichotomy including the strict epsilon equality. Verified against numerical SVD calculations for many dimensions; tests are nonproof supplements.

value.rationale: The precise perturbation scale at which m possible spectral components cease to be resolvably separate is a naturally motivated quantitative invariant of the emerging weighted-composition spectral-component problem. The theorem furnishes a sharp all-m infinite-to-finite resolvent reduction and a complete 2-component topological cutoff, with strict improvement over the normal case, rather than a cosmetic substitution or a finite table.
